judgment: A woman given in marriage: good.
It is good to hold firm.
image: Trees on the mountain: Step by Step.
So the noble one stays in worthy virtue
lines: Wild geese come step by step to the shore.
The small boy is in danger,
and there is talk, but no harm.
Wild geese come step by step to the great rock.
They eat and drink, at ease, at ease.
Good.
Wild geese come step by step to the dry land.
The husband marches and does not come back;
the wife conceives but does not bear. Misfortune.
It is good to fend raiders off.
Wild geese come step by step to the trees.
Perhaps they find a flat branch.
No harm.
Wild geese come step by step to the mound.
For three years the wife does not conceive,
but in the end nothing overcomes her.
Good.
Wild geese come step by step to the high road.
Their feathers can be used for the dancing.
Good.

notes.name_en: 漸 is advance by degrees (as water soaks in); 'Step by Step', not Wilhelm's 'Gradual Progress'. The phrase is carried into every goose line.
notes.L6: 逵 a broad high road; 羽…為儀 feathers used in ceremonial dance.
